newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks rocket, then flare out to close down.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks rocket, then flare out to close down.

text.p: Taiwan's stock index rocketed to within 300 points of 10,000 but hit heavy profit-taking in an extremely volatile final hour that erased the day's gains and sent the index to a lower close on record turnover.
Brokers nevertheless said they expected the index to recover in the near term and again to test stiff technical and psychological resistance at 9,600 points.

The broad weighted index, which soared 1.26 percent to a seven-year intraday high 9,714.78 at the open, gyrated wildly in the final hour of trade, dipping sharply on heavy profit-taking to as low as 9,451.45, a 1.48 percent downturn.
By the time the fireworks had ended and the smoke had cleared, the index had clawed its way back and pared its losses to just 37.56 points or 0.39 percent to close at 9,555.98.

Turnover shot to a historic high T$262.47 billion (US$9.4 billion) as investors defied the central bank's clear desire to cool down the rally, which many analysts attribute in large part to overly loose liquidity.
The bank has repeatedly issued negotiable certificates of desposit to tighten liquidity and slow a tide of cash into the stock market. On Tuesday, it said it issued T$8 billion worth.

Brokers attributed the volatile downturn mainly to strong final hour profit-taking sparked by the central bank's overt caution. Another factor was a tightening of margin-buying limits triggered by the index's push past 9,600.
"The pressure was too strong. Also, the central bank's moves to mop up excess funds were obvious," Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang said.

Defying the downturn was the crucial electronics sector, which has contributed some 60 percent of turnover in the big 1997 rally and ended Tuesday's session with a rise of 2.10 percent gain despite some late profit-taking.
